# Nuxt UI design system for Claude Design

A ready-to-import [Claude Design](https://claude.ai/design) design system that reproduces
[Nuxt UI](https://ui.nuxt.com) 4.11.1: components with their variants, sizes and colors, in
the light and the dark theme.

**The kit — everything in [`kit/`](kit/) — was generated by Claude Design** from the
`@nuxt/ui` sources (themes and Vue templates), and then checked against the real library:

- every theme value — slots, variants, compound variants, defaults — is compared with the
  library's resolved themes;
- 158 bench pages in two themes, 316 pairs of static screenshots, are compared pixel by
  pixel: one side rendered by the kit, the other by a Nuxt app built on `@nuxt/ui`. Every
  pair matches, or is covered by one of the known limitations listed below.

## Quick start

1. Get the kit: clone this repository or use **Code → Download ZIP**. The kit is the
   [`kit/`](kit/) folder, 425 files. For an earlier Nuxt UI version, take the matching
   [tag](#versions) instead of `main`.
2. Import it into Claude Design: [docs/import.md](docs/import.md).
3. Check the import: [docs/import.md#verify](docs/import.md#verify).

## Versions

Each release is a git tag named after the Nuxt UI version the kit reproduces: `v4.11.1` is
the kit for `@nuxt/ui` 4.11.1. `main` holds the latest one. If the kit is exported again for
the same Nuxt UI version, the tag moves to the new release: `v4.11.1` always points at the
latest kit for `@nuxt/ui` 4.11.1.

Project-level theme overrides (`app.config.ts`) are not part of the kit: it reproduces the
library as shipped.

## Known limitations

Differences found by the comparison and accepted on purpose. Each one is described in
[`bench/ledger.yaml`](bench/ledger.yaml) — classes with `status: accepted`, field `reason`.

- **Static components.** Overlays (menus, modals, popovers, tooltips) have no behavior: the
  open state is a prop. Hover states are not reproduced, and two hover rules
  (`group-hover:ring-primary`, `group-hover/blog-post:shadow-none`) do not match the
  library.
- **Not in the kit:** `ChangelogVersion`, `ChangelogVersions`, `PricingPlan`,
  `PricingPlans`, `PricingTable`, the `ColorMode*` components except `ColorModeSelect`,
  `LocaleSelect`, the `Content*` components for `@nuxt/content` and the `Prose*`
  typography. The Nuxt UI documentation shows how they look.
- **Editor** has no Tiptap inside: it is a static stand-in, the ProseMirror classes sit on
  the root, and there is no `content` node.
- **Toaster:** stacked toasts are laid out in normal flow with a gap, not positioned
  absolutely with transforms. The stack looks close, not identical. The progress bar is
  always full: the kit has no timer.
- **ContextMenu, open panel:** not checked. The library cannot render an open
  `UContextMenu` statically, so its two pairs are left out of the comparison.
- **Icons** are loaded at runtime from the Iconify CDN (`iconify-icon`), while the library
  uses the installed `@iconify-json/lucide`. Today every pair with icons matches; if the
  Lucide set on the CDN moves ahead of the package, glyphs may drift. Without network
  access the kit shows no icons.
- **Drawer with snap points:** the kit paints the overlay, the library does not.
- **CommandPalette:** its `Kbd` gets a slot name the library does not have. No visual effect.
- **Anti-aliasing:** a few pixels on rounded corners (Badge, DashboardNavbar,
  DashboardToolbar, a Drawer button) differ. Accepted as rendering noise.

## How it is built

- [`pipeline/`](pipeline/) builds the package Claude Design generates the kit from, exports
  the kit from the platform, and checks the kit's themes against the library.
- [`bench/`](bench/) is the visual comparison bench: a Nuxt app with one page per
  component, the matching kit artboards, and the ledger of differences.

Maintainer documentation is in Russian: [pipeline/README.md](pipeline/README.md),
[bench/README.md](bench/README.md).
